symbols.name: real numerator
symbols.meaning: The integer multiplier of $2^{-p}$ in the real part of a grid value.
symbols.quote: A grid value of precision $p$ has real and imaginary parts that are integer multiples of $2^{-p}$, so it has the form $2^{-p}(\sigma_1+i\sigma_2)$ with $\sigma_1,\sigma_2\in\mathbb{Z}$ the integer multipliers of the real and imaginary parts.

symbols.name: imaginary numerator
symbols.meaning: The integer multiplier of $2^{-p}$ in the imaginary part of a grid value.
symbols.quote: A grid value of precision $p$ has real and imaginary parts that are integer multiples of $2^{-p}$, so it has the form $2^{-p}(\sigma_1+i\sigma_2)$ with $\sigma_1,\sigma_2\in\mathbb{Z}$ the integer multipliers of the real and imaginary parts.

symbols.name: output coefficient
symbols.meaning: One output coefficient of the paper's polynomial multiplication, a sum of $r$ signed products of input coefficients.
symbols.quote: In the paper's polynomial multiplication, $W$ denotes one output coefficient (the paper's $H_j$).

symbols.name: truncation toward zero
symbols.meaning: The map that sends a real number to the integer nearest to it on the side of 0.
symbols.quote: Here $\mathrm{trunc}_0$ replaces a real number by the integer nearest to it on the side of $0$, so $\mathrm{trunc}_0(-2.7)=-2$.

symbols.name: word width
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in a signed word that stores one component numerator.
symbols.quote: A signed two's-complement word of $J$ bits, where $J$ is the number of bits, holds every integer from $-2^{J-1}$ to $2^{J-1}-1$

relations.quote: A grid numerator is the numerator of a [Gaussian dyadic](gaussian-dyadics.md) with denominator $2^p$.
Each grid numerator is an input to [carry propagation](carry-propagation.md), which converts integer coefficients into a binary string.
